You have not navigated in cloud, so this option assumes marked trails only and a route you can exit if visibility drops. Access needs were not answered, so I could not account for them. I have not checked the season, so it is left null. Confirm hut openings, trail conditions and any closures with Sépaq, the operator of Parc national de la Gaspésie. This is an option to consider, not clearance to go.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hut stay with a day-walk limit of 16 km
candidatesAccepted.summary: A shorter hut-based option that keeps daily walking under your 16 km ceiling and stays on established paths, which suits a party with some hut experience. Access needs were not answered and the season was not checked, so both are left unknown. Verify hut availability, trail status and route closures with Sépaq before relying on any of this. Nothing here is clearance to go.

candidatesAccepted.title: Reserve the park's backcountry hut nights before anything else
candidatesAccepted.summary: Hut nights in the park are the spine of this trip and the hardest thing to get late, so confirming a three-night reservation through the park operator is the first paperwork to settle. Access needs were not answered, so the reservation should be checked for accessibility of hut routes before you commit, and cloud navigation is not something this candidate addresses.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hire a handheld GPS or satellite messenger for the cloud problem
candidatesAccepted.summary: You have said you would rather not learn to navigate in cloud on this trip, and a rented GPS with a preloaded park map or a satellite messenger covers that gap without relying on phone signal, which is unreliable in these mountains. I have not checked rental availability or device models, so treat the price band as a rough guess and confirm with the shop.

candidatesAccepted.title: Check travel insurance that covers backcountry rescue
candidatesAccepted.summary: Hut-to-hut travel in remote terrain makes rescue cover the item most worth verifying before departure, since standard policies often exclude backcountry evacuation. I have not checked any specific policy's terms, and I could not account for access needs, which may change what cover is required.

gaps.detail: This part of the plan was left out to keep the run inside its budget. Re-planning with a larger budget would fill it in.
Nothing was checked about where to eat.
